- [RCTS.1.2.35] **`files`** (optional, `compiler` fixtures only) — an object
  mapping a path to the text of a `.dstest` file, which a harness must place
  beside the program or a library, so that a fixture can give a module its
  companion, or put a file beside it that is no module's companion
  ([LTSL.2.4]). A path is one or more segments joined by `/`, each one or more
  ASCII letters, digits and `_`, not beginning with a digit; the last is
  followed by `.dstest`.

  A harness must compile a fixture that carries `files`, and every
  `dsc_test_cases` fixture ([RCTS.1.2.10]), from files on disk, with the
  compiler's own `compile` ([RCLI.1.2]), so that which `.dstest` files the
  compile reads is the compiler's choice and not the harness's. In an empty
  directory D it must write the program as `D/main.ds`, each `libraries` entry
  as the file [LIMP.3.1.4] resolves its name to under `D/lib`
  ([RCTS.1.2.13]), and each `files` entry at its path under D. It must then
  compile `D/main.ds` with `D/lib` on the search path, the standard library
  after it ([RCTS.1.2.14]), and its dialects registered ([NDLC.2.1]). The
  program is compiled as written, with no `use` line supplied, so its `use`
  line is its own ([LDIA.2.10.1]).

  A harness must fail a fixture that carries `files` and whose category is
  not `compiler`, or whose `expect.kind` is not `compile_ok`, `compile_error`
  or `dsc_test_cases`. It must fail one whose `files` is not an object whose
  every value is a string, or names a path in another form, and a fixture it
  compiles from files whose program has no `use` line.
